sources.note: Bibliographic only. References for Chenchu [cde]: Trivedi 1978 (grammar), Bhūmani et al. 2015 (grammar sketch), Fürer-Haimendorf 1943 (ethnographic; pp. 284-285 cited for subclassification), Dick 1991 'Chenchu' in Encyclopedia of World Cultures vol. 3 South Asia pp. 61-62 (ethnographic), Khan 1941 'The Chenchus' in Essays presented to S. C. Roy pp. 161-164 (ethnographic). Glottolog annotates both Trivedi 1978 and Dick 1991 as 'Chenchu speak a dialect of Telugu'.

Segment inventory only (70 segments); no remark on stress or tone. The reference shown on the inventory page (Jacques 2011, Lingua, on Pumi aspirated fricatives) is evidently a database error and is not a Chenchu source.
No phonology; classifies Chenchu in the Telugu branch; cites only Ethnologue, Zvelebil 1990 and Krishnamurti 2003 (neither of which is a Chenchu description).

sources.citation: Fürer-Haimendorf, Christoph von. 1943. The Chenchus: Jungle Folk of the Deccan (The Aboriginal Tribes of Hyderabad, vol. I). London: Macmillan.
sources.note: Nothing. Ethnography; pp. 5-6 (Introduction) say 'Chenchus speak today a dialect of Telugu interspersed with a number of Urdu words' and that names/texts are 'transcribed phonetically without consideration of Telugu orthography.. consonants.. with their value in English and vowels with their value in Italian'; the idiom 'varies considerably both in pronunciation and phraseology from standard Telugu'. a full-text search for stress/accent the whole scanned text for stress/accent/intonation finds only non-linguistic uses ('times of stress').

sources.citation: Bhūmani, Ravīndra, Dāsari, Cinna Mūganna & Guravayya, Tōkala. 2015. Cenculu. In Ainavolu Usha Devi & D. Chandrasekhara Reddy (eds.), Āndhraprādēś Telaṅgāṇa Rāṣṭrāla bhāṣālu [Languages of the Andhra Pradesh and Telangana states], 375-396. Hyderabad: Emesco Books. [in Telugu]

sources.note: The only full description of Chenchu (phonology + morphology + texts, per the publisher blurb; Glottolog type 'grammar'; Grambank's sole source). Its phonology chapter is the one place a Chenchu stress statement is likely to exist. Digitized at HathiTrust (three copies) but in copyright, search-only; Harvard print copy Widener Library (offsite storage) PL4779.T74 (a scan can be requested through your own library).
